assumptions: Records are 16 bytes and sorted by key in the callers' use; the leaf itself does not check sortedness, and an unsorted array returns whatever the loop lands on, as the native code would.
A null element pointer, a null key-holder pointer, or a record array shorter than the byte span would be read unchecked by the native code; the model raises BisectLeafError for those inputs instead.
The 14 direct call sites are recorded as sites only; the containing functions and the target key each caller passes are not modelled here.

0x5f6bbbf.rule: byte diff <= 0 (signed) -> return begin without reading any record

0x5f6bc03.rule: half == 0 on the high side -> return lo

fields.key_chain: key = [[record]]: record first qword is an element pointer, key is the first qword at that address

semantics.comparison: unsigned: key >= target takes the high-side branch (native cmp + jae)
semantics.count: count = (end - begin) >> 4, arithmetic shift on the wrapping 64-bit byte difference; a non-positive signed difference returns begin without reading any record
semantics.loop: half = remaining >> 1; mid = lo + half; key >= target and half == 0 -> return lo; key >= target -> remaining = half; key < target -> remaining = remaining - half - 1, lo = mid + 1, continue while remaining > 0, else return lo
semantics.result: record pointer: first record whose key >= target, or one past the last record examined when every examined key is below the target; for a well-formed array that is the lower bound or the end pointer
